correctness.rationale: First-step elimination gives A_s f_{j+1}-B_s f_j+C_s f_{j-1}=0 with f_0=1 and f_{N-1}=b_gamma f_N. In particular b_gamma=1+(s/k_d)(1+lambda_+/(s+lambda_-+gamma)). Strict ordering also follows directly: the derivative of the killed resolvent equation with respect to gamma has forcing f_N-g_N>0 in row (N,a) only, and every transient state reaches that row, so the inverse resolvent makes every component strictly positive. This does not use criticality. At criticality A_0=C_0=D(lambda_++lambda_-), and B_s-A_s-C_s=s(s+lambda_++lambda_-). With s=sigma/N^2 the roots are 1±h/N+O(N^-2). The two cap coefficients in the frozen solution are asymptotic to he^-h/N and -he^h/N, giving the reflected-Brownian transform. For the difference between walls, the boundary forcing is (b_1-b_2)f_N(b_2) at N-1 minus b_1 times N, with b_1-b_2 asymptotic to sigma(delta_1-delta_2)/N^2 for distinct walls. On the difference basis z_+^j-z_-^j this boundary operator is -2h cosh(h)/N to leading order, while f_N(b_2) tends to sech(h). This gives the sign, the cosh(h)^2 denominator, and the factor sinh(hx)/h. Adjacent differences of this wall contrast are O(N^-2), so the active-state equation has the same scaled limit. At s=0 differentiation yields the slope recurrence d_{j+1}=d_j-1/D with d_N=delta_gamma; summation and the active backward equation give (3) and both mean differences. These arguments include x=1, gamma=0, and the trivial equal-wall contrast; they do not assert stochastic ordering. Supporting verifier was inspected, not executed. A fresh direct-generator check at N=9 and rates (k_d,k_e,lambda_+,lambda_-)=(2,3,1,1.5) corroborated all-state transform ordering at s=0.4 for gamma 0, 1 and 3 and the shortening means.
